Promotion of Art and Architecture
During the Golden Period of the Muslims,
Islamic art and architecture grew with the
discovery of new methods and technologies.
With conquest on new lands and increasing
influence of other civilizations,the Muslims
had new sources of inspiration.However, the
Muslim artisans improvedtheir own aesthetics
and createda whole new art style that is unique
HouseofWisdom (Bait ul Hikmah) in Baghdad
to thelslamic world.
In fact, during the Abbasid period, Muslim styles of art, architecture and literature
developed significantly. Great artists and architects made contributions under the
patronage of caliph. Not only original Arab literature thrived but Greek, Persian and
Sanskrit texts were translated into Arabic. Magnificent masjids were built by skilful
architects during this period. Craftsmen showed their skill at making brilliant pots,
glassware, fabrics, leather, and objects made of silver, copper and bronze.
Poetry
Most of the Arab world's most famous literary figures have been poets. Just like in the
courts of Damascus, in Baghdad too, poets were held in the highest of regard. Ibn Nuwas
and Al-Mutanabbi were two pf the most famous Arab court poets during Abbasid
caliphate.The Revival of Religious Sciences by Ghazali is yet another marvel and one of
themostquotedtexts.
In Persian language,OmarKhayyam wrote his famous Rubayyiat which is very famous in
the west too. The great poet Firdousi wrote his poetry during tenth and eleventh
century.
